## Useful command examples

### Create a new file:

```bash
cat <<'EOF' > newfile.py
import numpy as np
hello = "world"
print(hello)
EOF
```

### Edit files with sed:```bash
# Replace all occurrences
sed -i 's/old_string/new_string/g' filename.py

# Replace only first occurrence
sed -i 's/old_string/new_string/' filename.py

# Replace first occurrence on line 1
sed -i '1s/old_string/new_string/' filename.py

# Replace all occurrences in lines 1-10
sed -i '1,10s/old_string/new_string/g' filename.py
```

### View file content:

```bash
# View specific lines with numbers
nl -ba filename.py | sed -n '10,20p'
```

### Any other command you want to run

```bash
anything
```

        # dict of log name -> log level
        self._initial_logger_levels = {}  # type: Dict[Optional[str], int]

        self._initial_handler_level = None  # type: Optional[int]
        # dict of log name -> log level
        self._initial_logger_levels = {}  # type: Dict[Optional[str], int]

old_fin = '''        # restore log levels
        for logger_name, level in self._initial_logger_levels.items():
            logger = logging.getLogger(logger_name)
            logger.setLevel(level)
'''
new_fin = '''        # restore log levels
        if self._initial_handler_level is not None:
            self.handler.setLevel(self._initial_handler_level)

        for logger_name, level in self._initial_logger_levels.items():
            logger = logging.getLogger(logger_name)
            logger.setLevel(level)

old_set = '''        logger_obj.setLevel(level)
        self.handler.setLevel(level)

new_set = '''        logger_obj.setLevel(level)

        # save the original handler level to restore it during teardown;
        # only record the first value so repeated calls do not clobber it.
        if self._initial_handler_level is None:
            self._initial_handler_level = self.handler.level

        self._initial_handler_level = None  # type: Optional[int]
        # dict of log name -> log level

'''

        for logger_name, level in self._initial_logger_levels.items():
            logger = logging.getLogger(logger_name)
            logger.setLevel(level)
'''
new_fin = '''        # restore log levels
        if self._initial_handler_level is not None:
            self.handler.setLevel(self._initial_handler_level)

        for logger_name, level in self._initial_logger_levels.items():
            logger = logging.getLogger(logger_name)
            logger.setLevel(level)
'''

old_set = '''        logger_obj.setLevel(level)
        self.handler.setLevel(level)

new_set = '''        logger_obj.setLevel(level)

        # save the original handler level to restore it during teardown;
        # only record the first value so repeated calls do not clobber it.
        if self._initial_handler_level is None:
            self._initial_handler_level = self.handler.level
        self.handler.setLevel(level)

        self._initial_handler_level = None  # type: Optional[int]
        # dict of log name -> log level

'''
assert old_init in s, "init block not found"

        for logger_name, level in self._initial_logger_levels.items():
            logger = logging.getLogger(logger_name)
            logger.setLevel(level)
'''
new_fin = '''        # restore log levels
        if self._initial_handler_level is not None:
            self.handler.setLevel(self._initial_handler_level)

        for logger_name, level in self._initial_logger_levels.items():
            logger = logging.getLogger(logger_name)
            logger.setLevel(level)
'''

        self.handler.setLevel(level)

        # save the original handler level to restore it during teardown;
        # only record the first value so repeated calls do not clobber it.
        if self._initial_handler_level is None:
            self._initial_handler_level = self.handler.level
